speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your blood pressure, could you please tell me your age and if you have any symptoms like headaches, nosebleeds, or vision changes? I would also like to know if anyone in your family has had high blood pressure at a young age.

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given that secondary hypertension is common in children this age, I need to check for signs of renal artery stenosis or coarctation of the aorta. Is there any difference in blood pressure readings between his upper and lower extremities, and do you hear any abdominal bruits during examination?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the isolated hypertension in the upper extremity and the high suspicion for coarctation of the aorta, I will proceed with imaging. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let's compare the blood pressure readings between his right arm and left leg to check for a significant gradient. I will also listen for any murmurs or bruits over the chest and back to further evaluate for coarctation.

speaker: Patient
text: All systems review is essentially negative as reported by the mother.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to confirm the physical exam findings to rule out coarctation of the aorta. Can you tell me if there is a significant difference between the systolic blood pressure in his right arm and his left leg, and did you feel a delay or weakness in his femoral pulses compared to his radial pulses?

speaker: Patient
text: All systems review is essentially negative as reported by the mother.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the history is non-contributory, I must rely on objective physical exam data to differentiate between coarctation of the aorta and renal artery stenosis. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Pressure_Arm_vs_Leg, REQUEST TEST: Femoral_Pulse_Palpation

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Upper extremity blood pressure is 150/80 mm Hg with lower values in the lower extremities; femoral pulses are trace.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood pressure gradient and weak femoral pulses strongly suggest coarctation of the aorta. I will request imaging to confirm the anatomical narrowing. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: The echocardiogram confirms the narrowing of the aorta, which aligns perfectly with the clinical findings of upper extremity hypertension and weak femoral pulses. DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta
